2. Smt.Fathima Aneesha was married to one Muhammad Anas.
They have a male child.
Smt.Fathima Aneesha was found dead by hanging on 22.12.2020.

Tenhipalam Police Station was registered 2024:KER:83636 for unnatural death.
After collecting further materials, an offence under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) was initially added and an offence under Section 306 of the IPC was later incorporated.
The grievance of the petitioner is that there had been incessant demand for dowry by the husband, Sri.Mohammad Anas and his relatives.
The deceased was subjected to mental and physical cruelty in order to achieve their sinister motive of getting more dowry.
The said aspects were apprised.
But the investigating officer and the officials did not give any heed to the said facts.
Instead, the investigating officer proceeded with the investigation whimsically and thereby the offence of dowry death was not slapped against Sri.Mohammad Anas and his relatives.
More alarmingly, the investigating agency did not care to record the statement of the petitioner and other witnesses, which the petitioner wanted to bring before the court.
In such circumstances, the petitioner wanted investigation by a special team under the 2nd respondent.
The 6th respondent filed a statement explaining the steps taken in the matter of investigation.
The stand taken by the 6th respondent is that all the witnesses necessary to establish the guilt of the accused were collected and placed before the court.

Now, the offences alleged against the accused,
who are husband of the deceased and his parents, are punishable under Sections 498A and 306 read with Section 34 of the IPC.
A final report was already submitted before the court.
Pointing out the said circumstances, the 6 th respondent contended that the writ petition was devoid of any merit.
4. The petitioner has filed a reply-affidavit controverting the case of the 6 th respondent.
It is stated even that the claim of filing of final report is incorrect inasmuch as the petitioner was denied a copy of the same by the trial court stating that no such final report was filed.
The reply-affidavit was filed as early as on 01.12.2021.

5. The learned counsel for the petitioner now submits that the final report was already submitted,
the matter was 2024:KER:83636 committed and it is pending before the Sessions Court, Manjeri.
The matter is now listed for hearing to decide whether or not a charge is liable to be framed.

The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that having the matter progressed to that extent,
entrusting the investigation with a different agency may not be feasible, although the grievance of the petitioner remains unredressed.

6. True, when the petitioner has an allegation that there were continuous harassment and meting out of cruelty against Smt.Fathima Aneesha and the death occurred within three years of the date of marriage, the investigating agency ought to have had an investigation so as to ascertain whether an offence under Section 304B of the IPC also was committed.

In the light of the provisions of Section 113B of the Evidence Act, 1872, the investigating agency did have an obligation to ascertain whether the offence under Section 304B of the IPC would be attracted since the death was within seven years of date of marriage.
7. Be that as it may, the proceedings for prosecuting the husband and his parents are now pending before the trial 2024:KER:83636 court.

At such a stage, it is inappropriate and against the interest Ashraf.V vs The State Of Kerala on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130812874/
3 of justice to hand over the investigation to a different agency.

sentences.text: If at all required a further investigation has to be resorted to and that can be had only by the same agency.
Similarly, the grievance of the petitioner can be redressed by filing a private complaint alleging additional offences and citing the witnesses, whom he wanted to examine.
Equally, it is possible for the Public Prosecutor in charge of the case to apprise the trial court about the possibility of adding offence under Section 304B of the IPC in the charge.

Without prejudice to the said rights of the petitioner,
this writ petition is liable to be disposed of.
Accordingly, the writ petition is disposed of without prejudice to the aforementioned rights of the petitioner.

Sd/-

This writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India was filed by the father of the deceased, Smt.Fathima Aneesha seeking the following reliefs:
"i) Issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ or order directing the 2nd respondent to hand over the investigation in Crime No.606/2020 registered at Tenhipalam Police Station in Malappuram District to the Crime Branch;
ii) Issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ or order directing the 2nd respondent to constitute a Special Team of Police Officers holding unblemished record in the field of investigation for investigating Crime No.606/2020 registered at Tenhipalam Police Station and to submit final report within a time frame as fixed by this Hon'ble Court."
